grade.rationale: The component is concise and generally correct, but date formatting can throw on malformed API values and the hand-built focus trap can select elements that are not actually tabbable. The remaining logic is readable and reasonably testable, although browser globals and formatting helpers warrant focused unit tests.

summary: Two robustness issues were identified: invalid date strings can break template rendering, and the focus-trap selector does not reliably model the browser's tab order. Test coverage is unknown because no coverage data was supplied.

grade.rationale: The aggregation, expansion, and duration logic is straightforward, but focus traversal can fail when the selected boundary element cannot receive focus.
The implementation is compact and well named, though maintaining a custom focus trap requires accounting for many browser focusability rules.
Methods and computed values have clear purposes, with simple control flow and descriptive names.
Malformed date values are passed directly to Intl formatters, which can throw RangeError and disrupt rendering instead of producing a safe fallback.
Most helpers are deterministic, but focus behavior depends directly on document state and queued microtasks. Coverage is unknown rather than assumed absent.

findings.title: Invalid date values can throw during rendering
findings.description: Both date helpers construct a Date and immediately pass it to Intl.DateTimeFormat.format(). If an API value is empty, malformed, or otherwise invalid, format() throws a RangeError. When these methods are invoked from the template, one bad usage record can interrupt change detection and prevent the history view from rendering.
findings.recommendation: Parse and validate the date before formatting, for example by checking Number.isNaN(date.getTime()), and return a consistent fallback such as "Unavailable" for invalid values. Add tests covering malformed, empty, and valid timestamp/day inputs.

findings.title: Focus trap can target elements outside the sequential tab order
findings.description: The selector includes hidden elements and any tabindex except the literal value -1, including negative values such as -2. Calling focus() on an invisible candidate may do nothing, while focusing another negative-tabindex candidate introduces it into keyboard traversal unexpectedly. Either case can make the modal's Tab boundary behavior inconsistent or allow focus to escape.
findings.recommendation: Use a proven dialog/focus-trap primitive, or filter candidates for visibility, inert/disabled state, and a non-negative effective tabIndex before choosing the first and last elements. Add keyboard tests for hidden controls, negative tabindex values, forward Tab, and Shift+Tab.
